title: The module-valued exchange of a composite base change is the composite of the exchanges
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y_1\to Y$ and $k:Y_2\to Y_1$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\square_1=(f,f_1,g,g_1)$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f_1:X_1\to Y_1$, $g_1:X_1\to X$, $fg_1=gf_1$, and let $\square_2=(f_1,f_2,k,k_1)$ be a cartesian square with $f_2:X_2\to Y_2$, $k_1:X_2\to X_1$, $f_1k_1=kf_2$; the outer rectangle $\square_2\cdot\square_1=(f,f_2,g\circ k,g_1\circ k_1)$ is then a cartesian square [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. Use the constant-coefficient module sheaves and unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the exact inverse images $u^{-1}$ on module sheaves [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and their termwise derived functors, the derived direct images $Ru_*$ and the derived adjunctions $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$, and the unbounded module exchange morphisms $\Ex_\square:g^{-1}Rf_*\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}$, all as specified in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] (these are the derived base-change maps of [sbc-def-base-change-map] on the exchanged squares). For morphisms $u:V\to W$, $v:V'\to V$ let $c^\Lambda_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$ be the isomorphism of functors $D(W_{\Et},\Lambda)\to D(V'_{\Et},\Lambda)$ obtained by applying termwise the sheaf composition isomorphism $c_{u,v}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2), which is $\Lambda$-linear for the module structures of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2), and descending it along the localizations. Then, as natural transformations $(g\circ k)^{-1}Rf_*\to Rf_{2*}(g_1\circ k_1)^{-1}$ of functors $D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to D(Y_{2,\Et},\Lambda)$,
$$
\Ex_{\square_2\cdot\square_1}=(Rf_{2*}c^\Lambda_{g_1,k_1})\circ(\Ex_{\square_2}g_1^{-1})\circ(k^{-1}\Ex_{\square_1})\circ((c^\Lambda_{g,k})^{-1}Rf_*):
$$
$$
(gk)^{-1}Rf_*\to k^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*\to k^{-1}Rf_{1*}g_1^{-1}\to Rf_{2*}k_1^{-1}g_1^{-1}\to Rf_{2*}(g_1k_1)^{-1}.
$$
In particular, $\Ex_{\square_2\cdot\square_1,K}$ is an isomorphism if and only if $\Ex_{\square_2,g_1^{-1}K}\circ k^{-1}\Ex_{\square_1,K}$ is one.
